capabilities.note: A rollout is service-reported and shifts traffic only after each batch passes its health check.
The last healthy artifact can be restored without rebuilding it.
Unhealthy instances can be replaced while healthy instances continue serving traffic.
A repository and region can be registered before a first deployment.
An on-call engineer records resolution only after checking service recovery.
Incident updates are persisted in an ordered timeline.
Region, auto-deploy and notification preferences persist through an explicit save.
A failed rollout email points to the persisted attempt and its diagnostic values.
An opted-in on-call engineer receives a notification for the recorded incident.
Automatic rollback or incident resolution is not offered; each recovery operation requires an engineer’s explicit action.

rollbackReviewEvent.label: Review restoration of the previous artifact

flows.goal: Inspect a service record, review an artifact and follow its health-gated rollout.
flows.ends: The artifact’s rollout is recorded as Complete with measured service recovery; the engineer can revisit the attempt and its owner.

flows.goal: Investigate the billing incident, restore its last healthy artifact and record verified recovery.
flows.ends: The previous artifact is serving with passing health checks and the incident is persisted as Resolved with its investigation timeline intact.

flows.goal: Inspect a failed build and explicitly retry the same artifact.
flows.ends: The failed attempt remains inspectable and the retried rollout reports its own accepted completion.

flows.goal: Replace unhealthy notification instances after reviewing the current artifact.
flows.ends: Replacement instances report passing health checks while the incident remains open for on-call verification.

flows.goal: Register a repository and region before choosing the service’s first artifact.
flows.ends: A registered service and stable record route exist; registration alone does not claim a successful deployment.

binding.because: Repository, region and deploy preferences form a deliberate registration draft distinct from observed telemetry.

flows.goal: Add an observation to the on-call investigation without issuing a deployment from chat.
flows.ends: The accepted observation is visible in timestamp order and its composer draft is cleared only after persistence.

flows.goal: Save default region, auto-deploy and failure or health notifications.
flows.ends: Saved preferences apply to later registrations and notifications without rewriting existing rollout attempts.

flows.goal: Read batch safety and artifact reuse rules before choosing recovery.
flows.ends: The engineer understands health-gated traffic shifts and that rollback restores rather than rebuilds an artifact.

flows.goal: Open the exact failed rollout from its email diagnostics.
flows.ends: The persisted failed artifact, build exit code and duration are visible before an explicit retry.

flows.goal: Open a recorded incident from an on-call notification.
flows.ends: The notified incident opens with its affected service, owner and investigation timeline.

flows.goal: Understand health-gated deployments and enter the service-health overview.
flows.ends: The engineer reaches measured service health rather than an unsupported automatic-remediation or signup flow.

product.outcome: Deploy a registered service, follow its reported rollout, and resolve a health incident only after the service has recovered.

users.who: An on-call engineer selecting artifacts, reviewing rollout failures and recording recovery with the team.
A teammate checking service health and rollout progress without initiating a recovery.

homeReady.label: Current health
homeReady.rule: Show measured request, latency, error and deployment dimensions with sample times; incidents link to their affected service.

homeLoading.label: Refreshing health
homeLoading.rule: Keep the last measured health and incident list visible with their timestamps while requesting fresh observations.

homeEmpty.label: No registered services
homeEmpty.rule: Show no metrics or incidents and direct the engineer to register a repository.

homeFailed.label: Health unavailable
homeFailed.rule: Report a failed health request, not a failed deploy; do not invent zero metrics or healthy status.

homeLongContent.label: Long incident and service names
homeLongContent.rule: Wrap full service identity and incident evidence without separating an incident from its affected service.

servicesReady.label: Registered services
servicesReady.rule: Show each service’s health, region, latest measured latency and last deployment time; opening the record exposes its rollout history.

servicesLoading.label: Refreshing services
servicesLoading.rule: Retain known service rows and timestamps while refreshing health.

servicesEmpty.label: No registered services
servicesEmpty.rule: Offer repository registration; a service is not healthy until it has reported observations.

servicesFailed.label: Services unavailable
servicesFailed.rule: Retry the registry request without reporting it as a build failure.

servicesLongContent.label: Long service identity
servicesLongContent.rule: Wrap the regional billing worker name without hiding its region or health.

servicesMinutes.label: Recent deployment
servicesMinutes.rule: Show a minute-relative deployment time computed from the service’s ISO timestamp.

servicesHours.label: Deployment hours ago
servicesHours.rule: Show an hour-relative deployment time computed from the service’s ISO timestamp.

servicesDays.label: Deployment days ago
servicesDays.rule: Show a day-relative deployment time computed from the service’s ISO timestamp.

servicesWeeks.label: Deployment weeks ago
servicesWeeks.rule: Show a week-relative deployment time computed from the service’s ISO timestamp.

serviceDetailReady.label: Service record
serviceDetailReady.rule: Show billing’s current health, configuration, selected artifact and rollout diagnostics before any operation.

serviceDetailLoading.label: Refreshing record
serviceDetailLoading.rule: Retain the selected service and current artifact while refreshing; withhold deployment and recovery controls until refreshed.

serviceDetailEmpty.label: Service removed
serviceDetailEmpty.rule: Show the missing registered service and a route to the registry; do not create a new service with the old route.

serviceDetailFailed.label: Record unavailable
serviceDetailFailed.rule: Report a failed record request separately from a persisted deploy failure; no rollout actions are available.

serviceDetailLongContent.label: Long service and artifact names
serviceDetailLongContent.rule: Wrap the complete regional service and release artifact names beside their configuration.

serviceDetailDeploying.label: Rolling out
serviceDetailDeploying.rule: Keep the selected artifact and measured batch progress visible, lock conflicting recovery operations and prevent duplicate rollout submission.

serviceDetailDeployed.label: Rollout complete
serviceDetailDeployed.rule: Show all batches complete and billing health recovered; do not mark an incident resolved automatically.

serviceDetailDeployFailed.label: Deploy failed
serviceDetailDeployFailed.rule: Show persisted build exit code and duration, retain the previous serving artifact, and offer explicit retry of the failed artifact.

serviceDetailRollingBack.label: Rolling back
serviceDetailRollingBack.rule: Restore the last healthy artifact without rebuilding; keep the current service record visible and prevent another recovery operation.

serviceDetailRolledBack.label: Rollback complete
serviceDetailRolledBack.rule: Show restored artifact and passing health checks; leave the incident open for the on-call engineer to verify.

serviceDetailRollbackFailed.label: Rollback failed
serviceDetailRollbackFailed.rule: Show the failed health check and keep the currently active artifact serving; offer retry without claiming restoration.

serviceDetailRestarting.label: Restarting instances
serviceDetailRestarting.rule: Replace unhealthy notification instances while healthy instances stay active; lock duplicate restart.

serviceDetailRestarted.label: Instances restarted
serviceDetailRestarted.rule: Show healthy replacement instances and passing checks, leaving incident resolution to the engineer.

serviceDetailRestartFailed.label: Restart failed
serviceDetailRestartFailed.rule: Keep known healthy instances serving and show that replacement health checks failed; offer explicit restart retry.

deploysReady.label: Rollout history
deploysReady.rule: Group persisted rollout attempts by their service-reported stage; stages are not editable task columns.

deploysLoading.label: Refreshing rollout history
deploysLoading.rule: Keep known attempts and their progress visible while fetching reported updates.

deploysEmpty.label: No rollout attempts
deploysEmpty.rule: Route to a registered service to select its first artifact; do not offer moving a card to invent a deployment.

deploysFailed.label: Rollout history unavailable
deploysFailed.rule: Retry reading history without retrying the deployments themselves.

deploysLongContent.label: Long release artifact
deploysLongContent.rule: Wrap the complete artifact identifier with its service and owner before its reported progress.

incidentsReady.label: Open incidents
incidentsReady.rule: Show each recorded incident with its affected service and on-call owner; opening one preserves the investigation context.

incidentsLoading.label: Refreshing incidents
incidentsLoading.rule: Keep known incidents and owners visible while fetching changes.

incidentsEmpty.label: No open incidents
incidentsEmpty.rule: State only that no incidents are recorded; do not equate an empty incident list with measured healthy services.

incidentsFailed.label: Incidents unavailable
incidentsFailed.rule: Retry reading the incident register without opening a duplicate incident.

incidentsLongContent.label: Long incident evidence
incidentsLongContent.rule: Wrap the complete incident title and report with its affected service and owner.

incidentsResolved.label: Resolved incident
incidentsResolved.rule: Keep the resolved incident and its timeline available for the next on-call handoff.

incidentThreadReady.label: Incident timeline
incidentThreadReady.rule: Show the billing incident, affected service and observations in timestamp order; recovery operations are performed on the service record.

incidentThreadLoading.label: Refreshing timeline
incidentThreadLoading.rule: Retain the incident context and existing observations while requesting newer updates.

incidentThreadEmpty.label: No observations
incidentThreadEmpty.rule: Keep the recorded incident and affected service visible and invite the first on-call observation.

incidentThreadFailed.label: Timeline unavailable
incidentThreadFailed.rule: Keep the incident and service context visible and retry reading observations without sending a duplicate update.

incidentThreadLongContent.label: Long recovery observation
incidentThreadLongContent.rule: Wrap the full diagnostic observation and on-call identity without replacing the incident context.

incidentThreadSending.label: Sending observation
incidentThreadSending.rule: Retain the authored observation and prevent duplicate sending until the timeline accepts it.

incidentThreadSent.label: Observation recorded
incidentThreadSent.rule: Append the persisted observation and clear the composer only after acceptance.

incidentThreadSendFailed.label: Observation not sent
incidentThreadSendFailed.rule: Keep the unsent observation and offer Send update again.

incidentThreadRecovered.label: Service recovered
incidentThreadRecovered.rule: Show passing service health alongside the still-open incident so the engineer can review resolution explicitly.

incidentThreadResolving.label: Recording resolution
incidentThreadResolving.rule: Keep recovery evidence visible and disable duplicate resolution while recording the incident outcome.

incidentThreadResolved.label: Incident resolved
incidentThreadResolved.rule: Show the persisted resolved state and retain the timeline for handoff; do not offer resolving it again.

incidentThreadResolveFailed.label: Resolution not recorded
incidentThreadResolveFailed.rule: Keep the recovered service visible and the incident open; allow an explicit retry of resolution.

newServiceDraft.label: Registration draft
newServiceDraft.rule: Edit the repository, name and region only; health, latency and deployment timestamps are observed later, never entered into this form.

newServiceSaving.label: Registering service
newServiceSaving.rule: Keep the complete registration draft and disable duplicate registration while persisting the repository.

newServiceSaved.label: Service registered
newServiceSaved.rule: Replace the registration form with the newly registered service and a route to choose its first artifact.

newServiceFailed.label: Registration failed
newServiceFailed.rule: Retain the full repository and region draft, and retry registration without claiming a service or deploy exists.

newServiceLongContent.label: Long repository name
newServiceLongContent.rule: Keep the full repository and service name editable and wrap them before the region controls.

settingsReady.label: Editable
settingsReady.rule: Keep the saved default region, auto-deploy and failure or health alert preferences visible; changes apply only after Save preferences.

settingsSaving.label: Saving
settingsSaving.rule: Keep changed preferences visible, disable Save, and announce the in-flight persistence operation.

settingsSaved.label: Saved
settingsSaved.rule: Show the persisted preference values and an inline acknowledgement without leaving settings.

settingsFailed.label: Save failed
settingsFailed.rule: Retain unsaved operations preferences and explain that the previous region and notification settings still apply; allow an explicit save retry.

helpReady.label: Rollout safety guide
helpReady.rule: Explain batch health gates and artifact reuse before an engineer chooses deployment or rollback.

landingReady.label: Operations introduction
landingReady.rule: Explain service records, health-gated rollouts and incident timelines; link only to modelled operations surfaces.

emailDeployFailedReady.label: Recorded rollout failure
emailDeployFailedReady.rule: Send only for the persisted failed billing rollout; include its artifact, exit code and duration and open that attempt rather than retrying automatically.

pushIncidentOpenedReady.label: Incident recorded
pushIncidentOpenedReady.rule: Notify the opted-in on-call engineer only after the billing incident is recorded with an affected service and owner.

serviceDetailRegistered.label: Registered, not deployed
serviceDetailRegistered.rule: Show the registered repository and region without health, latency, last-deploy time or a serving artifact. The selected first artifact can be reviewed before starting a rollout.

serviceDetailNotifications.label: Notification service record
serviceDetailNotifications.rule: Show the down notification service and its current artifact before reviewing replacement of unhealthy instances; do not offer manual rollout-stage editing.

surfaces.question: Which service has a measured health exception, and which incident explains the next investigation?

binding.because: On-call work starts with exceptions and recorded incidents rather than a launcher of unrelated tools.

surfaces.question: Which registered service changed health, and when was its last deployment?
Which artifact is serving this service, why did the rollout fail, and is deploy, rollback or restart the safe next operation?

slots.because: Each reviewed operation identifies the service and artifact before it can change serving traffic.

surfaces.question: Which artifact and owner belong to each recorded rollout attempt, and what stage has the service reported?
Which recorded incident is open, which service is affected, and who is on call?
What evidence explains this service incident, what has the on-call team tried, and has recovery been recorded?

slots.because: Resolution changes the incident’s recorded state only after an engineer has reviewed measured recovery.
The recorded resolution belongs beside the incident timeline and must survive a transient notification.

binding.because: On-call observations need the incident identity, owner and measured service recovery alongside the timeline.

surfaces.question: Which repository, service name and region should be registered before the first artifact is deployed?

binding.because: Registering a repository, supported region and deploy preferences is a deliberate draft, separate from observed service telemetry.

surfaces.question: Which default region, auto-deploy behavior and operational notifications do I want saved?

binding.because: Default region, auto-deploy and failure or health notifications belong to one small on-call preference page.
